autodir.tagline: MatchFrame moves the CS2 camera for you.

pov.label: Player POVs
pov.hint: Always on: follows the action and switches players.

cinematic.label: Cinematic cameras
cinematic.hint: Team shots and spawn cameras in freeze time, the bomb at plant and defuse, and overviews of big fights. Built-in cameras for every active-duty map.

nade.label: Nade cams
nade.hint: Cameras that catch smokes, flashes, molotovs and HE grenades as they land (Full Action Observer).
nade.hintTop: Nade cams come with the top plan. Upgrade on the website.

chase.label: Chase cam
chase.hint: Shows the player from behind (third person) while they plant or defuse the bomb and when their team wins the round, then goes back to their eyes.

clutch.label: Clutch mode
clutch.hint: When one player is left alone against the other team, stay with them: no cuts to cameras, and the chase view while no opponent is near. A won clutch is replayed if automatic replays are on.

variety.label: Different freeze times
variety.hint: Not the same shots every round: sometimes one longer shot of one team, from high up, low or from their side; no team shot of a team saving on an eco; cameras used in the last rounds give way to others.

big.label: Big moments
big.hint: A wide opener before each pistol round, the team on match point first and longer, and slow shots of the map at half time and at the end of the map (the winners first).

winners.label: After the round, show the winners

hlae.label: Camera shots through HLAE
hlae.hint: With CS2 started in the Observer tools + HLAE mode, HLAE plays every camera shot and move: it sets the view every frame, so turns, glides and paths are smooth and don't depend on console timing. The map's camera paths (200–300 a map, from pro demos) play in freeze time only while HLAE is connected. Without HLAE, MatchFrame moves the camera over the console.

standard.label: Standard
standard.detail: CS2 through Steam with the game data (GSI) config. Works on any server. No console: camera control uses the keyboard fallback, or none.

tools.label: Observer tools
tools.detail: Adds -tools -netconport: MatchFrame controls the camera and the game options below through CS2's console. Needs the free CS2 Workshop Tools (Steam → Counter-Strike 2 → DLC).

hlae.label: Observer tools + HLAE
hlae.detail: Also loads HLAE (advancedfx) for no flash, team colours in the kill feed or no game kill feed at all, and no end-of-match scene. CS2 runs insecure: only LAN, demos, or servers with tv_secure_bypass 1.

hlaeWarning.w1: HLAE (advancedfx) hooks into CS2, and CS2 then runs with -insecure.
hlaeWarning.w2: Insecure CS2 cannot join VAC-secured servers: the match server must allow insecure observers (tv_secure_bypass 1), or use LAN or demos.
hlaeWarning.w3: Never join matchmaking or a VAC-secured server while HLAE is loaded: HLAE's developers warn this can get the account VAC banned.
hlaeWarning.w4: CS2 updates often break HLAE until HLAE is updated. Standard and Observer tools keep working.

opt.label: Game options
opt.frameCapHint: fps_max: CS2 draws at most this many frames a second, leaving the graphics card room for the HUD, OBS and the encoder. On high graphics settings an uncapped CS2 takes the whole card, and imported HUDs stutter. For a 60 fps stream, 120 keeps the game smooth. Don't change: CS2's own setting.
opt.coloursHint: The colours for the X-ray, smokes and the kill feed. Your CT and T colours stay with the side; each team's colour (Teams → colour) swaps with the teams at half time, and a team without one uses yours.
opt.hideHudHint: cl_drawhud 1 and cl_draw_only_deathnotices 1: the game shows only its kill feed (and, with X-ray, the names above the players); your HUD shows the rest. Sent when the console connects.
opt.xrayHint: spec_show_xray, hud_showtargetid and cl_drawhud_force_teamid_overhead: players visible through walls on the observer's screen, with their names above them (also with Hide game HUD on).
opt.clutchXrayHint: When one player is left against two or more, X-ray goes off until the round ends, so the viewer doesn't see where the other team is. It comes back on for the next round.
opt.retakeXrayHint: After the plant, once a CT is close to the bomb with time left to defuse and both teams still have players alive, X-ray goes off until the round ends, so the viewer doesn't see where the Ts wait. Not while the CTs save.
opt.backgroundHint: engine_no_focus_sleep 0 and snd_mute_losefocus 0: CS2 keeps every frame and its sound while you use MatchFrame or OBS. Off, CS2 slows down and goes silent whenever another window has focus. With CS2 in full screen (not Fullscreen Windowed), clicking another window still stops the picture.
opt.noFlashHint: HLAE mirv_noflash 1: flashbangs don't white out the observer's screen.
opt.xrayColoursHint: HLAE mirv_colors: the players' glow through walls (X-ray), the names above them and grenade trails in the CT and T colours below. Only in your game: the players don't see it. The glow changes from the next switch of player; trails from the next grenade.
opt.smokesHint: HLAE mirv_colors smokes: smokes in the CT and T colours below, from the next smoke thrown. Only in your game: the players don't see it.
opt.killfeedColoursHint: HLAE mirv_deathmsg colors: CT and T names in CS2's kill feed in the CT and T colours below.
opt.endOfMatchHint: HLAE mirv_endofmatch 0: no end-of-match scene over the game.
opt.hideKillfeedHint: HLAE mirv_deathmsg filter add block=1: CS2's own kill feed is blocked, so only your HUD's kill feed shows. With Hide game HUD on, the crosshair stays.

prod.obsSceneSceneWithThe: OBS: scene “{scene}” with the media source “{input}” is ready{v}

prod.noClipsKeptForIt: No clips kept for it yet.
prod.noClipOfItHas: No clip of it has been played yet.
prod.eachHighlightSlowedAsAutomatic: Each highlight slowed as automatic replays slow theirs (around each kill when theirs is off); a kill's extra angle slowed after it, its first angle at real time.
prod.theBestOfTheMap: The best of the map's other clips (the replay PC films more than a break has time for).
prod.bestByTheSameScore: Best: by the same score as automatic replays.

prod.onceTheRoundSReplays: Once the round's replays are over, and only when the program is on the live scene: never over your own scene.

prod.theLastHalfOfThis: The last half of this map

prod.whereReelsGoAndThe: Where reels go, and the clips kept
prod.noClipsToPutIn: No clips to put in the reel

prod.noClipsOfThisMap: No clips of this map yet.
prod.noClipOfThisMap: No clip of this map has been played yet.
prod.eachClipSlowedAsAutomatic: Each clip slowed as automatic replays slow theirs (around each kill when theirs is off); a kill's extra angle slowed after it, the first angle at real time.

prod.bestByTheSameScore2: Best: by the same score as the automatic replays.

prod.playerCardOnALong: Player card on a long player view
prod.shownByThemselvesWhileThe: Shown by themselves while the Auto Director has the camera.
prod.fromHighlightsBackToThe: From highlights back to the scene the program came from (or to live).
prod.toHighlightsOnAirFrom: To highlights on air, from the scene the program is on.

prod.toAndFromTheBreak: To and from the break and studio scenes: by themselves (above) or with your program buttons.
prod.fromAReplayBackTo: From a replay back to live, also after a replay played by hand and Return live.
prod.fromTheLiveSceneTo: From the live scene to a replay.
prod.whenAMapEndsThen: When a map ends, then back to the live scene when the next map starts.
prod.onATacticalTimeoutOr: On a tactical timeout or a technical pause, then back to the live scene when play resumes.
prod.connectObsInSettingsDevices2: Connect OBS in Settings → Devices to pick scenes.
prod.whichObsSceneIsOn: Which OBS scene is on program, and when it changes by itself.

reasons.thisReasonCodeIsNewer: This reason code is newer than this console.
reasons.freezeTimeOneTeamSaves: Freeze time: one team saves while the other has a full buy. Both teams are shown, the full buy last.
reasons.freezeTimeATeamSpent: Freeze time: a team spent what it had without a full buy. Its shot comes last and longer, close enough to see the pistols or SMGs.
reasons.clutchTheShortLookAt: Clutch: the short look at an opponent is over; back to the clutcher, the clutch's default view.
reasons.clutchAnOpponentIsAbout: Clutch: an opponent is about to meet the clutcher (in sight, a sightline opening, or a few steps away), so the camera is back on the clutcher.
reasons.clutchAShortLookAt: Clutch: a short look at an opponent starting to defuse the bomb.
reasons.clutchAShortLookAt2: Clutch: a short look at an opponent starting to plant the bomb.
reasons.clutchAShortLookAt3: Clutch: a short look at an opponent walking into the bombsite the clutcher holds.
reasons.clutchAShortLook2: Clutch: a short look (2–4 s) at an opponent walking in on the clutcher, then back to the clutcher before they meet.
reasons.theEndOfTheMap: The end of the map: the winners first, then slow shots of the map.
reasons.slowShotsOfTheMap: Slow shots of the map and the teams during half time, the team ahead first.
reasons.aTeamIsOneRound: A team is one round from winning the map: its team shot comes first and runs longer.
reasons.freezeTimeBeforeAPistol: Freeze time before a pistol round: it opens wide with the map's camera, then the teams.
reasons.aShortShotOfThe: A short shot of the team that won the round, where they stand, 2 s after the round ends.
reasons.justGotAKillStill: Just got a kill, still alive, with enemies close: another kill often follows, so the director stays on (or goes to) this player.
reasons.aPlayerIsRunningSomewhere: A player is running somewhere with no fight close: a free camera can fly behind them.
reasons.replayPcTheMainPc: Replay PC: the main PC already shows this player, so this computer films someone else.
reasons.noUsableShotWasFound: No usable shot was found; holding.
reasons.aTacticalOrTechnicalPause: A tactical or technical pause: a still shot of one team's spawn until the round goes live.
reasons.anEstablishingShotToOrient: An establishing shot to orient viewers.
reasons.partOfTheRoundS: Part of the round's main storyline.
reasons.playersAreSeparatedByGeometry: Players are separated by geometry; contact is less likely.
reasons.theOperatorAskedTheDirector: The operator asked the director to hold the current shot.
reasons.theOperatorPinnedAPlayer: The operator pinned a player/side; candidates are restricted.
reasons.theOperatorOwnsTheCamera: The operator owns the camera; the director only recommends.
reasons.telemetryIsStaleAutomatedDecisions: Telemetry is stale; automated decisions are unsafe.
reasons.aRecentlyAbandonedShotIs: A recently abandoned shot is cooling down.
reasons.theCameraHasNotBeen: The camera has not been validated on this map revision/build.
reasons.thisShotTypeIsNot: This shot type is not part of the selected Observer mode (nade cameras need Full Action Observer; cinematics need Observer & Cinematics).
reasons.aCinematicWasCutShort: A cinematic was cut short by more important action.
reasons.aCinematicCameraShotIs: A cinematic camera shot is available.
reasons.cinematicsAreDisabledForThis: Cinematics are disabled for this round/map/match.
reasons.thePerRoundCinematicBudget: The per-round cinematic budget is used up.
reasons.noValidatedStaticCameraCovers: No validated static camera covers the utility; falling back to POV/radar/hold.
reasons.theUtilityIsUnlikelyTo: The utility is unlikely to matter on screen.
reasons.utilityIsLandingOnA: Utility is landing on a group of players.
reasons.aLonePlayerIsPushing: A lone player is pushing aggressively.
reasons.theTargetIsReadyTo: The target is ready to fight (weapon ready, not flashed).

replays.theSourceInYourReplay: The source in your replay scene that plays clips

replays.connectObsOnThisComputer: Connect OBS on this computer (Settings → Devices); its replay buffer starts by itself. Or let the main PC record this screen over NDI (its Replay feed).

Only when no kill loses its lead-up: with 7 s behind, after the round ends here. Needs going back to work (a CSTV connection).
replays.onlyKillsTheMainCamera: Only kills the main camera missed
replays.behindTheMainPcThis: Behind the main PC, this computer can film every kill it has time for; the main PC replays the best of each round.
replays.goBackForEachMissed: Go back for each missed kill, then live
replays.onTheSameCstvAs: On the same CSTV as the main PC
replays.aCodeIsSavedType: A code is saved; type a new one to replace it.
replays.asShownOnTheMain: As shown on the main PC, e.g. 192.168.1.20:37211
replays.typeTheMainPcS2: Type the main PC's address and its replay PC code below.
replays.onThisComputerStartCs2: On this computer: Start CS2 and spectate the same match, connect OBS (Game Capture of CS2) and start the Auto Director.
replays.noFramesLostInThe: No frames lost in the last 10 s.
replays.tofixedSKeptTofixed2V: {toFixed} s kept · {toFixed2}{v} frames a second arriving · {clips} clips cut
replays.startTheNdiSenderOn: Start the NDI sender on the replay PC first, then find it here.
replays.theRecordingNeedsFfmpegInstall: The recording needs ffmpeg: install it with this system's package manager.
replays.theRecordingNeedsFfmpegA: The recording needs ffmpeg (a 92 MB download from gyan.dev, checked before use).
replays.itKeepsTheLastFew: It keeps the last few minutes and cuts clips from them; nothing is played from it by itself.
replays.thisComputerRecordsTheReplay: This computer records the replay PC's whole screen over NDI and cuts each kill from it. The replay PC then needs no OBS: only an NDI screen sender, such as vMix Desktop Capture.
replays.shownOnceRemoveItIn: Shown once. Remove it in Settings → Access to lock the replay PC out.
replays.replayPcCodeMadeType: Replay PC code made: type it on the replay PC
replays.onlyThisComputerCanConnect: Only this computer can connect right now.
replays.thisComputerHasNoNetwork: This computer has no network address. Connect it to the same network as the replay PC.
replays.thisComputerSAddressUse: This computer's address (use one the replay PC can reach):
replays.networkAccessIsSetIn: Network access is set in the MatchFrame program on the main PC.
replays.theyStillNeedACode: They still need a code from this computer. Windows may ask to allow MatchFrame through the firewall: allow it on private networks.
replays.letOtherComputersOnThe: Let other computers on the network connect
replays.makeAReplayPcCode2: Make a replay PC code and type it, with this computer's address, on the replay PC.
replays.letOtherComputersConnectTo: Let other computers connect to this one.
replays.theEngineRestartsTheConsole: The engine restarts; the console reconnects by itself.
replays.aSecondComputerWithIts: A second computer with its own CS2 and OBS that films the kills this camera misses.
replays.mainPcOnCstvGive: Main PC on CSTV: give the server a second CSTV, 7 s later than the first, and connect to it here (connect server-address:27021). With the main CSTV at tv_delay 10:{div}
replays.mainPcInTheServer: Main PC in the server as a spectator: watch the server's CSTV here, with a CSTV delay of about 7 s (tv_delay 7).
replays.bothOnTheSameCstv: Both on the same CSTV: nothing to set up. This computer goes back 7 s by itself (demo_gototick -448 relative) and stays there (below).
replays.thenEveryKillTheMain: Then every kill the main camera misses is known here before it happens on this computer: the camera gets on the killer first and the whole kill is filmed. The program measures how far behind it is by itself.
replays.bestThisComputerAbout7: Best: this computer about 7 s behind the main PC
replays.thisComputerFilmsSomeoneElse: This computer films someone else and sends what its camera happens to catch.
replays.whenAKillTheMain: When a kill the main camera missed wasn't on this camera, CS2 goes back a few seconds, films it, then skips forward to live again.
replays.globalHotkeysWorkWithCs2: Global hotkeys work with CS2 or OBS in front. They are off until set; the suggested keys aren't used by CS2 or OBS.
replays.inTheConsoleJoinStream: In the console: {join}. Stream Deck and Bitfocus Companion: {devices}.
replays.theDeviceActionsReplaySkip: the device actions replay_skip, replay_hold, replay_stop, replay_exclude and replay_pin (see the Replay PC guide)
replays.someStepsFailedSeeFix: Some steps failed: see Fix above, then test again.
replays.playsTwoSampleClipsThrough: Plays two sample clips through the same path as a break's replays. Not while a round is live.
replays.thisPlaysOnYourProgram: This plays on your program output now: two sample clips (Test clip 1 and 2) with Replay in, the fade between them and Replay out, the live game audio turned down meanwhile. It takes about 10 seconds.
replays.replaysCarryTheReplayPc: Replays carry the replay PC's game sound: the replay feed records it with the picture (when its NDI sender sends sound), and clips from its OBS replay buffer have the tracks its OBS records.
replays.theLiveGameAudioTick: The live game audio: tick the {v} with the game's sound. Only these are touched: leave casters' microphones unticked.
replays.turnedDownWithAShort: Turned down with a short ramp as the replays start, and back to exactly where it was after them, however they end.
replays.bothReplayMediaSourcesYour: Both replay media sources (your replay scene's and its copy). Above 0 dB is louder than recorded.
replays.eachReplayInputInVmix: Each replay input in vMix (its fader; above 0 dB its gain).
replays.extraAngleAskedOfThe: Extra angle asked of the replay PC: {join}
replays.askTheReplayPcFor: Ask the replay PC for this kill's extra angles, and play them with it
replays.starredItsExtraAnglesAre: Starred: its extra angles are asked for and play with it
replays.playsAtRealTimePress: Plays at real time: press for slow motion
replays.playsInSlowMotionPress: Plays in slow motion: press for real time
replays.thisBreakPlaysAsOne: . This break plays as one rendered file: Exclude, Pin and Slow made now apply from the next break.
replays.clipsOfTheRoundBest: Clips of the round, best first
replays.fadesBetweenReplaysThroughScene: Fades between replays through “{scene}”, a copy of your replay scene that MatchFrame keeps the same: leave it to MatchFrame.
replays.addsAMatchframeReplayScene: Adds a “MatchFrame Replay” scene to OBS and uses it, with a second one beside it for fading between replays. Pick a Stinger for replays under OBS scenes → Transitions.
replays.obsSceneSceneWithThe: OBS: scene “{scene}” with the media source “{input}” is ready
replays.eachReplayIsAddedTo: Each replay is added to vMix as an input (the next one while the one before plays) and removed after the break's replays.
replays.backToLiveAfterThe: Back to live after the last replay.
replays.toTheFirstReplayStingers: To the first replay. Stingers use vMix's own Stinger 1 or 2.
replays.vmixOnThisComputerWith: vMix on this computer, with its Web Controller on (vMix → Settings → Web Controller).
replays.whenTheMainCameraShows: When the main camera shows a 3K or more, save this computer's OBS replay buffer and replay it too.
replays.whenTheMainCameraShowed: When the main camera showed only the player who died, replay it from the killer's side (from the replay PC).
replays.theRoundSTopKill: The round's top kill and starred kills
replays.theReplayPcIsAsked: The replay PC is asked to film the moment again from another angle (it goes back in its CS2 when that costs no kill: Replay PC → Film extra angles). An angle that arrives in time plays straight after the moment, slowed, when the break has time for it. Star a clip in the list below to ask for its angles and play them with it.
replays.makesTheInBetweenFrames: Makes the in-between frames by motion interpolation instead of blending two frames. It takes far longer (measured: about half a second a frame at 1080p on a 4-core CPU without a graphics card), so a break uses it only when its file will still be ready in time; highlights and reels, which can wait, always do.
replays.mutedTheGameSoundFades: Muted: the game sound fades out just before the slow part and back in after it (clean; casters talk over it). Slowed: played slower with its pitch kept, which can make gunshots sound doubled.
replays.killMomentEachClipEases: Kill moment: each clip eases down to the slow speed about 0.3 s before its kill, holds through it and eases back up after (each kill of a multi-kill). The break's clips are chosen with the longer lengths, so they still end in time.
replays.killMomentSlowsARendered: Kill moment slows a rendered break's file: played clip by clip (vMix, or Fade (two scenes, OBS)) only Whole clip is slowed, by the mixer.
replays.aRenderedBreakSSound: A rendered break's sound fades in at its start and out at its end, so it never ends on a hard cut (and before Stop or the round clock ends it early).
replays.fadeOneSceneRenderedThe: Fade (one scene, rendered): the break's clips are joined into one file with the fade and played in your replay scene; smoothest, needs ffmpeg (Replay feed). Fade (two scenes, OBS): each clip in your replay scene and a copy of it, OBS fading between them. If the file isn't ready in time, the break plays the second way.
replays.theEndOfOneReplay: The end of one replay fades into the start of the next (vMix's Fade), or a cut.
replays.replaysMayRunOnInto: Replays may run on into the next round while the teams leave spawn: the cut back to live starts by this time on its clock (CS2's round starts at 1:55). The bomb planted, or the round over, ends them at once.
replays.theChosenClipsPlayBack: The chosen clips play back to back. Round order: from the start of the round to its end. Best first: the best one first.
replays.theBestClipsOfThe: The best clips of the round that fit in the break; the rest are left.
replays.whileEarlyReplaysAreOn: While early replays are on air: a CT back within reach of a defuse, a duel, a kill, or a T within reach of a plant.
replays.backToLiveIfThe: Back to live if the round isn't over after all
replays.beforeTheBombGoesOff: Before the bomb goes off, or before the round clock ends. 10 s is the most.
replays.theBombIsPlantedAnd: The bomb is planted and no CT can reach it and defuse in time, or no T can plant before the round clock ends, and no duel is on or about to start. Never with more than 10 s left on the bomb or the round clock.
replays.startReplaysEarlyWhenThe: Start replays early when the round is decided
replays.justBeforeTheNextRound: just before the next round starts
replays.inTheBreakAfterA: In the break after a round: from a few seconds after it ends until {v}, one transition to the replays and one back to live. They never start once the next round is live.
replays.heldNothingPlaysOnUntil: Held: nothing plays on until Resume. The round clock still cuts back to live.
replays.backToTheLiveScene: Back to the live scene now, with Replay out ({shortcutLabel})
replays.endsTheClipOnAir: Ends the clip on air now ({shortcutLabel})
replays.newFilesGoToThe: New files go to the new folder from then on. Clips already saved stay where they are and still play and go into reels. A folder on another drive (D:, an SSD for video) keeps this load off the drive Windows is on.
replays.whereReplaysAndHighlightsAre: Where replays and highlights are saved on this computer

replays.folderForReplayClipsAnd: Folder for replay clips and the replay feed's recording

setup.staticCameraRecordedAsPartial: Static camera recorded as partial support

setup.fromTheSimulationNotA: From the simulation, not a real CS2 client

setup.gsiConfigAlreadyUpTo: GSI config already up to date
setup.requiredBecauseCs2WasNot: Required because CS2 was not detected

setup.labelledSimulationASynthetic5v5: Labelled simulation: a synthetic 5v5 on a synthetic map for rehearsals. It is always labelled and never certifies real telemetry or camera control.
